abstract: Knausgård (arXiv 2610.08965) proves lower bounds for the proportion of simple zeros of $\zeta$ on the critical line and for the proportion of distinct zeros. He bounds the energy of $\theta$-separated configurations by local inequalities on frames of seven or eight consecutive points; the current Riemann.fail records use ten. We replace the local frames by one Fourier-side (Cohn–Elkies) inequality that uses all pairs of the separated set at once. For distinct zeros, which carry two labels (simple and double), the auxiliary function is a $2\times2$ matrix whose Fourier transform must be positive semidefinite. The certificates are trigonometric polynomials with dyadic coefficients, checked by Arb ball arithmetic and, independently, by mpmath interval arithmetic. We obtain $\liminf N_0^s/N\ge0.6737629012$ and $\liminf N_d/N\ge0.8392652448$, against $0.6736388767$ (the Riemann.fail record, a ten-point certificate on the same window) and $0.8390046$ (Knausgård). The gains are small ($1.24\cdot10^{-4}$ and $2.61\cdot10^{-4}$). Through Knausgård's §6 the same certificates give $0.8368814$ for $(N_s+N_0)/2N$ and $0.8893325$ for the zeros that are simple or on the line. The main point of the note is where the bounds place the schemes. The critical-line certificate is within $8\cdot10^{-5}$ of the all-pairs ceiling for its window, and mobius_drift's numerical cap shows that no window in the level-2 scheme passes $0.67400$. For distinct zeros the smallest margin among the conditions is in the close-pair condition for two simple zeros (a candidate bottleneck), and raising the degree parameter from $m=32$ to $m=48$ gains only $5\cdot10^{-5}$ more (float). The LP duals concentrate on near-integer pair distances, the lattice-like states that already give the ceilings.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary: Version 2 answers the review. (1) Verifier B: the mpmath codes read interval endpoints through 53-bit round-to-nearest conversions and formed one endpoint difference outside interval arithmetic. They now read endpoints exactly at 128 bits and form the difference in interval arithmetic; corollaries_iv.py widens the enclosures it reads back by 1e-36. All reruns pass with the same bounds (0.673762901208596, 0.673761086693138, 0.83926524485288; corollaries unchanged); the lower bounds for beta move by about 3e-18. Section 4 records the defect and the fix. (2) Section 5 and the abstract no longer call the simple-simple close-pair condition binding: it is the smallest margin, a candidate bottleneck, not a sensitivity result. The statement that passing 0.6740 needs a different scheme is made conditional on the numerical cap [3]. The REC-window ceiling no longer truncates a tail: the periodic-state energies are now finite Poisson sums (R = f*f has support in [-1, 1]), and a new Arb script, ceiling_rec_arb.py, encloses the two-state LP value with upper end 0.67384183277, which is the quoted 0.6738418. Section 6 says the dual atoms suggest, but do not show, realisable or optimal near-lattice states. (3) Corollary 3 now quotes e0 - 1 - x1 >= 2.836. Section 7 now agrees with the status line (Theorem D read by an outside reader, scoped to the reduction). The label [U] is removed, and references are numbered. No theorem or certificate changed.
title: All-pairs Cohn–Elkies certificates in Knausgård's level-2 schemes: 67.376% simple zeros on the critical line, 83.926% distinct zeros, and how close the schemes are to their ceilings
